citation.authors: Lee SWH, Chen WS, Sellappans R, Md Sharif SB et al

cited_by.title: Fasting in Ramadan with diabetes or sickle cell

record.population: 5,359 Muslims with type 2 diabetes fasting in Ramadan, in 17 randomised trials of drugs or education
record.design: Cochrane systematic review of randomised trials, GRADE
record.finding: Every trial had at least one high-risk domain for bias. Dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitors may cause less hypoglycaemia than sulphonylureas (low-certainty evidence). The evidence on serious hypoglycaemia, other harms and HbA1c was very uncertain, and no deaths were reported. Trials compared medicines; none tested whether fasting itself is safe.
record.note: My copy of the abstract is cut before the education and insulin results and does not list the countries; strength is therefore taken at the lower reading.
